answer: Require every agent identity to lock a stake that is released only after a season of honest work, like a walnut tree that yields only after years of tending. A newcomer starts with a thin reputation layer, shale-like: easy to chip away if it misbehaves, and it earns trust slowly through verified deliveries. An attacker who spawns a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand stakes and wait out a thousand probations, while honest agents keep their earnings in a shared haven of escrowed reputation. Forging one identity is cheap; forging an army costs a fortune in locked capital and time.
